I met a problem on design of interraction of Ext and arbitrary semi-linear equiv as I want to prove the invariant of projective/injective dimension under arbitrary semi-linear equiv to show Gorenstein local ring is stable under ring equivlence. Here I not only met universe issue but also instance of module. (In contrast I think proving Localization is Gorenstein is relatively easier? I don't know why, maybe just an illusion.)
Our current setup: we know that Ext commute with flat base change when the ring is noetherian and the module on the left is finitely generated. See PR #30532.
The universe level needed is as follow:
For R in universe u and S in universe u' a flat R-algebra, assume R is v-small and S is v'-small with v not greater than v', for v \le w and v' \le w'
Ext.{w'} MS NS n is the base change of Ext.{w} M N n with S if MS and NS (in ModuleCat.{v'}) are base change of M and N (in ModuleCat.{v}) respectively.

Currently I have the following in mind:
I first construct the linear equiv of Ext under linear equiv of modules respectively. This can also be separated into two steps as I need UnivLE.{v, v'} at first.
Then consider change of ring only in the same universe. I have in mind that the two category at this time is equivalent? So we might be able to directly construct the map from two sides? If this is not ideal enough we are still able to consider using base change.
At last we connect the above two steps together to obtain a full universe invariant semi-linear equiv between Ext.

My guess is that if F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ is an exact fully faithful functor between abelian categories such that

  1. C₁ has enough projectives and F preserves projectives, or
  2. C₁ has enough injectives and F preserves injectives,
    then, the maps on Ext induced by F are bijections.
This can be applied for the ulift-functor on modules, or for the equivalence of categories given by extension or restriction of scalars by a ring isomorphism.

The right way to do all of this should probably be to define Ext-types attached to modules with generic universe parameters:

def Module.Ext (R : Type u) [Ring R] (M₁ : Type v₁) [AddCommGroup M₁]
    [Module R M₁] (M₂ : Type v₂) [AddCommGroup M₂] [Module R M₂] : Type (max u v₁ v₂) :=
  -- use the categorical `Ext` in the category `ModuleCat.{max u v₁ v₂} R`

Joël Riou 說：

My guess is that if F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ is an exact fully faithful functor between abelian categories such that

  1. C₁ has enough projectives and F preserves projectives, or
  2. C₁ has enough injectives and F preserves injectives,
    then, the maps on Ext induced by F are bijections.

The inverse can't be canonically constructed right? If so and I didn't get it wrong, this can be done by dimension shifting?

However sorry that I don't think I am fully ready for this general Module.Ext? As there may involve many redesigns? Also I think I don't need it for now (?) But if this is definitely needed then I am willing to do it as soon as possible before to much things are already built on Ext.

Nailin Guan said:

The inverse can't be canonically constructed right? If so and I didn't get it wrong, this can be done by dimension shifting?

The statement would be that the induced maps satisfy Function.Bijective, and this would hold by induction on the dimension.
I've opened #31697 for the bijection.

However I have some more question: I believe using restrict scalars with ring isomorphism is able to construct a category equivalence thus two sides of the isomorphism between Ext can be explicitly constructed?
But as I tried to prove the map between Ext is compatible with composition of exact functors, I found it a bit hard to prove by either using SmallShiftedHom.map or ShiftedHom.map. I am not very sure about what is missing?
If I didn't get it wrong, ModuleCat.uliftFunctor is missing? I try to add it in #31706
(deleted)
I've opened #31768 for compatibility with (semi-)linear equiv with general universe.

Digging this out, somebody is currently not satisfied with the commute of Ext and ULift and Ext under semi linear equivalences. I have an vague idea that we are able to move forward to Module.Ext proposed earlier? However, since we ULift is far from being canonical, we may still need to deal with NatIso between composition of them. This is technical obstacle.

The other obstacles are what are the APIs we want to port to Module.Ext, Ext.comp and the long exact sequence is probably in reach, however those related to Ext.mapExactFunctor would not be able to state easily anymore.

The last thing is about the math within it, for Ext in pure mathematics, we really treat it as some objects characterized by universal property, thus only properties invariance under isomorphisms, we may just don't really care about how the isomorphism is between different universes.

The definition of Module.Ext I suggested above only makes sense if it comes with a clean API, which I know would be very painful to do, but I do not think there are intermediate solutions.
The real question is: do we really need universe polymorphism?
I think that a formalization of local algebra where all the modules (and the ring) are in the same universe is good enough.

Some problem comes with change of rings, here the particular problem is the invariance of being Gorenstein (the ring itself has finite injective dimension) under ring isomorphism, do we have good idea about this?
I mostly agree with the suggestion to work with modules in the same universe, this works well most of the times.
Why not just formalizing the invariance of being Gorenstein under isomorphisms of rings in the same universe?
So you mean by the isomorphism of Ext under restricting scalars by a ring isomorphism still make sense?

In that case, do you not just need to know that the injective dimension of an object is invariant under an equivalence of categories? For categories of modules, this should follow from https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/Ext/MapBijective.html
I have that as a part of #31768, then I would remove other universe polymorphisms for now. Thanks for these suggestions.

Back to the Module.Ext issue, I was only wondering what APIs should be migrated to it. I only mean that those functor related stuffs may not be able to work anymore above Module.Ext. Since currently we only covered extend scalars and restrict scalars, if adding more we might need to touch the original Ext again.
I have some idea of making the ulift isomorphism somehow canonical, but I am not very sure about this is the correct way.
I don't think we should have Module.Ext, but instead improve the API for going between Module R M and M : ModuleCat R where necessary.

Nailin Guan said:

Back to the Module.Ext issue, I was only wondering what APIs should be migrated to it. I only mean that those functor related stuffs may not be able to work anymore above Module.Ext. Since currently we only covered extend scalars and restrict scalars, if adding more we might need to touch the original Ext again.

I am afraid it is extremely difficult to understand what you are trying to say.
In order to do Module.Ext cleanly, we would have to obtain the pseudo-functoriality properties of https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/ExactFunctor.html i.e. when we have two composable functors F and G between abelian categories, we can consider the composition of the functors on the derived categories, and it should be canonically isomorphic to the functor induced by the composition of the two exact functors, and then when we compose three functors, we have to show compatibilities between the various isomorphisms, etc. Then, show similar things for the compositions of induced maps on Ext-groups by several functors, and finally apply all of this to compositions of ULift/restriction of scalars functors between categories of modules. All of that is an extremely painful task, I would not like to encourage anybody to pursue in that direction.
Thanks for the suggestions (I probably mean instructions, sorry), there are many more obstacles that I didn't foresee.
These are not suggestions! Please focus on the "single" universe API as it is much much important from the mathematical point of view.
